title: Validate long-route browser performance and driving experience
acceptance: a production browser build can start directly in free driving, render real compiled NYC tiles, and complete representative long routes including at least one cross-borough route without a scene reload that breaks play

measured profiling records frame time, physics time, loaded tile count, active collider count, memory trend, and tile-load hitching while driving far enough that many tiles have been loaded and unloaded
memory/collider counts return toward a bounded steady state after leaving regions rather than growing monotonically with total distance traveled

human browser verification records that steering, braking, AWD grip/slip, handbrake drift initiation/recovery, wide miniature/isometric camera readability, reset, non-road support/fall recovery, minimap readability, and current-road identity are usable on the real road world
simplified scenery and road geography make representative NYC areas spatially recognizable without requiring photorealistic landmark art

production startup profiling records initial JS/WASM transfer size, parse/initialization time, and time-to-drive; the T007 baseline warning that Rapier is eagerly bundled (about 3.43 MB minified / 1.24 MB gzip in that build) is either accepted with evidence or addressed with practical code splitting
automated browser smoke coverage is added to .agent/VERIFY.json and required license/attribution notices are present in the distributable build
